To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of trips generated by commercial establishments is influenced by the establishment’s sector, its business size and its distance to the city centre.
the freight generation of commercial establishments in Gothenburg is mainly influenced by the type of business, business size and location.
the freight trip generation is determined by: (i) establishment’s sector; (ii) business size and location; and (iii) the number of employees and the number of customers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the freight needs and the traffic impacts of urban commercial establishments, which have been neglected in previous research.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
establishments’ freight trip generation and attraction is a complex phenomenon that is affected by several factors.
the freight needs of establishments vary considerably, both within and across sectors.
there are no general rules, but rather that the results are sector specific and depend on the type of goods sold and the business size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this paper contributes to the literature in two main ways: (i) it presents a comprehensive study of urban commercial establishments’ generation and attraction of freight trips and freight volumes and weights, and (ii) it introduces a set of models to estimate establishments’ freight trips, and freight volumes and weight, which can be used to support planning and policy design processes.
the models can be useful for policy makers and planners to better understand the freight generation of urban commercial establishments, and thus to better design and evaluate policies and plans.
the results show that the number of freight vehicles per week generated by an establishment can be predicted by the number of employees and establishment’s size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the models can be used for freight demand analysis in urban freight planning and policy design, as well as in urban freight forecasting and simulation.
the models can be used to estimate establishments’ freight needs in urban areas.
the freight generation and traffic impacts of commercial sectors can be estimated using data from establishments.
